cases.sentence: Еще чувствовалось в их отношениях к нему и сомнение о том, кто он такой (не очень ли ___), и враждебность вследствие еще свежей их личной борьбы с ним.
cases.explain: «важный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The officer and soldiers who had arrested Pierre treated him with hostility but yet with respect, in the guardhouse to which he was taken. In their attitude toward him could still be felt both uncertainty as to who he might be—perhaps a very important person—and hostility as a result of their recent personal conflict with him.

cases.sentence: Но когда, в утро ___, пришла смена, то Пьер почувствовал, что для нового караула — для офицеров и солдат — он уже не имел того смысла, который имел для тех, которые его взяли.
cases.explain: «другого дня» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: But when the guard was relieved next morning, Pierre felt that for the new guard—both officers and men—he was not as interesting as he had been to his captors; and in fact the guard of the second day did not recognize in this big, stout man in a peasant coat the vigorous person who had fought so desperately with the marauder and the convoy and had uttered those solemn words about saving a child; they saw in him only No. 17 of the captured Russians, arrested and detained for some reason by order of the Higher Command. If they noticed anything remarkable about Pierre, it was only his unabashed, meditative concentration and thoughtfulness, and the way he spoke French, which struck them as surprisingly good. In spite of this he was placed that day with the other arrested suspects, as the separate room he had occupied was required by an officer.

cases.sentence: Несмотря на то, в тот же день Пьера соединили с другими взятыми ___, так как отдельная комната, которую он занимал, понадобилась офицеру.
cases.explain: «подозрительными людьми» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: But when the guard was relieved next morning, Pierre felt that for the new guard—both officers and men—he was not as interesting as he had been to his captors; and in fact the guard of the second day did not recognize in this big, stout man in a peasant coat the vigorous person who had fought so desperately with the marauder and the convoy and had uttered those solemn words about saving a child; they saw in him only No. 17 of the captured Russians, arrested and detained for some reason by order of the Higher Command. If they noticed anything remarkable about Pierre, it was only his unabashed, meditative concentration and thoughtfulness, and the way he spoke French, which struck them as surprisingly good. In spite of this he was placed that day with the other arrested suspects, as the separate room he had occupied was required by an officer.

cases.sentence: Все русские, содержавшиеся с Пьером, были люди самого ___.
cases.explain: «низкого звания» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: All the Russians confined with Pierre were men of the lowest class and, recognizing him as a gentleman, they all avoided him, more especially as he spoke French. Pierre felt sad at hearing them making fun of him.

cases.sentence: На ___ вечером Пьер узнал, что все эти содержащиеся (и вероятно он в том же числе) должны были быть судимы за поджигательство.
cases.explain: «другой день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: That evening he learned that all these prisoners (he, probably, among them) were to be tried for incendiarism. On the third day he was taken with the others to a house where a French general with a white mustache sat with two colonels and other Frenchmen with scarves on their arms. With the precision and definiteness customary in addressing prisoners, and which is supposed to preclude human frailty, Pierre like the others was questioned as to who he was, where he had been, with what object, and so on.

cases.sentence: На ___ Пьера водили с другими в какой-то дом, где сидели французский генерал с белыми усами, два полковника и другие французы с шарфами на руках.
cases.explain: «третий день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: That evening he learned that all these prisoners (he, probably, among them) were to be tried for incendiarism. On the third day he was taken with the others to a house where a French general with a white mustache sat with two colonels and other Frenchmen with scarves on their arms. With the precision and definiteness customary in addressing prisoners, and which is supposed to preclude human frailty, Pierre like the others was questioned as to who he was, where he had been, with what object, and so on.

cases.sentence: Пьеру, наравне с другими, делали с той, мнимо-превышающею ___, точностью и определительностью, с которою обыкновенно обращаются с подсудимыми, вопросы о том, кто он? где он был? с какою целью? и т. п.
cases.explain: «человеческие слабости» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: That evening he learned that all these prisoners (he, probably, among them) were to be tried for incendiarism. On the third day he was taken with the others to a house where a French general with a white mustache sat with two colonels and other Frenchmen with scarves on their arms. With the precision and definiteness customary in addressing prisoners, and which is supposed to preclude human frailty, Pierre like the others was questioned as to who he was, where he had been, with what object, and so on.

cases.sentence: Очень нехорошо, — строго сказал ему генерал с ___ и красным румяным лицом.
cases.explain: «белыми усами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Put that down, that’s bad … very bad,” sternly remarked the general with the white mustache and red flushed face.

cases.sentence: Пьера с 13-ю другими отвели на Крымский Брод в каретный сарай ___.
cases.explain: «купеческого дома» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Pierre and thirteen others were moved to the coach house of a merchant’s house near the Crimean bridge. On his way through the streets Pierre felt stifled by the smoke which seemed to hang over the whole city. Fires were visible on all sides. He did not then realize the significance of the burning of Moscow, and looked at the fires with horror.

cases.sentence: В ___ дома у Крымского Брода Пьер пробыл еще четыре дня и во время этих дней из разговора французских солдат узнал, что все, содержавшиеся здесь, ожидали с каждым днем решения маршала.
cases.explain: «каретном сарае» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: He passed four days in the coach house near the Crimean bridge and during that time learned, from the talk of the French soldiers, that all those confined there were awaiting a decision which might come any day from the marshal. What marshal this was, Pierre could not learn from the soldiers. Evidently for them “the marshal” represented a very high and rather mysterious power.

cases.sentence: Для солдата очевидно маршал представлялся высшим и несколько ___ власти.
cases.explain: «таинственным звеном» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: He passed four days in the coach house near the Crimean bridge and during that time learned, from the talk of the French soldiers, that all those confined there were awaiting a decision which might come any day from the marshal. What marshal this was, Pierre could not learn from the soldiers. Evidently for them “the marshal” represented a very high and rather mysterious power.
